reason: Full batch reviewed. Request one local repair covering three proof and statement issues; the affected consumers remain valid after the wording correction.

findings.reason: The Statement calls p_i=P_h(e_i/sqrt(lambda_i)) energy-orthonormal. In general A_h=I-G with a nonzero error Gram matrix G, so these vectors are a basis but not orthonormal. Remove the orthonormality claim; the small-gap hypothesis already supplies basis status.

Proof step 1.2 calls subsequential convergence the compact-operator definition, but the actual definition requires compact closure of bounded images. The sequential-compactness equivalence requires dependent choice in this library, while the example assumes only countable choice. Repair locally without strengthening assumptions: use finite-coordinate truncations and the uniform tail bound to show J(B_V) is totally bounded, then use completeness of its closure and the countable-choice complete-plus-totally-bounded theorem.

Proof step 2.1 asserts K_h is compact from finite dimensionality without giving the bridge to the compact-closure definition. State that K_h is bounded as a finite-dimensional linear map and apply Heine–Borel to the closure of its unit-ball image before invoking the compact spectral theorem.

consumer_checks.reason: Uses the Ritz-matrix quotient bound on U_h; its argument does not require the basis p_i to be orthonormal.
Uses the fixed-index eigenvalue bounds and discrete min–max; it does not rely on the inaccurate orthonormality description.
Its use of the corrected matrix statement is unaffected: in the example the approximation gap is zero. Its separate compactness-proof defect is listed above.
The page summary claims the matrix and no-collapse estimates, not that the projected vectors form an orthonormal basis.
Its companion summary does not use the inaccurate basis claim.
